objective: Build a simple responsive React Todo web app that supports adding, deleting, and completing tasks, persists tasks in localStorage, includes unit tests, and builds successfully with npm run build.
assumptions: Use the existing project tooling and conventions if present; otherwise initialize a minimal React project with Vite.
Tasks contain an id, text, and completed boolean.
Tasks are stored locally in the current browser; authentication, backend services, and cross-device synchronization are out of scope.
Marking a task completed is reversible through a checkbox.
requirements: Render a task input, Add button, task list, and an empty-state message.
Add a task through form submission, supporting both the Add button and Enter.
Trim task text and reject empty or whitespace-only submissions.
Delete an individual task without affecting other tasks.
Toggle each task between active and completed, with a visible completed state.
Restore tasks from localStorage on startup and persist additions, deletions, and completion changes.
Provide a basic responsive layout with accessible input labels, buttons, and checkboxes.
Include unit tests for task behavior and persistence.
Provide working npm test and npm run build scripts.
architecture: App owns task state, input state, and add, delete, and toggle handlers; keep the small task form and list in this component unless existing conventions favor extraction.
A small storage module loads, validates, and saves the task array under a stable namespaced localStorage key.
Initialize task state lazily from storage, then persist task changes through an effect.
Use stable unique task ids for React keys and mutations; never use array indexes as task identities.
Suggested files: src/App.jsx, src/App.test.jsx, src/taskStorage.js, src/taskStorage.test.js, src/styles.css, and a test setup file. Follow existing language and filename conventions.
Use existing test tooling when available; otherwise use Vitest, jsdom, React Testing Library, user-event, and jest-dom.
implementation_steps: Inspect package.json, source files, and repository instructions. Preserve existing configuration and add only missing React, build, or test setup.
Implement storage loading and saving with JSON parsing, task-shape validation, and exception handling. Return an empty array for missing or invalid stored data.
Implement task state with lazy storage initialization. Add immutable handlers for creating a uniquely identified task, deleting by id, and toggling completion by id.
Build the accessible form, task list, completion checkboxes, delete buttons, and empty state. Clear the input after successful submission.
Connect persistence to task-state changes so initial loading happens before any save.
Add minimal responsive CSS using a centered container, flexible controls, wrapping task text, and a visually distinct completed state.
Configure a non-watch npm test command and implement focused storage and component tests.
Run the full test suite and npm run build, resolve failures, and manually verify responsive behavior and persistence after reload.
edge_cases: Empty or whitespace-only input creates no task.
Duplicate task text is allowed; ids keep completion and deletion independent.
Long task text and unbroken strings wrap without causing horizontal overflow.
Deleting the final task restores the empty state and persists an empty array.
Missing, malformed, or structurally invalid stored data results in an empty task list without crashing.
Unavailable localStorage or a failed write does not prevent in-memory task operations.
Restored completed tasks retain their state, and initialization does not overwrite valid stored tasks with an empty array.
acceptance_criteria: The app uses React and displays an empty state when no tasks exist.
Submitting valid text by button or Enter adds exactly one incomplete task with trimmed text and clears the input.
Whitespace-only submissions do not change the list.
A completion checkbox toggles only its corresponding task and updates its visual state.
Deleting a task removes only that task, including when multiple tasks have identical text.
After reload, saved task text, order, and completion states are restored; deleted tasks remain absent.
Storage errors do not crash the app or disable task operations.
At 320px and desktop viewport widths, controls remain usable and task text does not cause horizontal overflow.
Inputs and controls have accessible names and support keyboard operation.
npm test passes without entering watch mode, and npm run build exits successfully.
verification_plan: Unit-test storage loading for missing data, valid tasks, malformed JSON, invalid task shapes, and storage read exceptions.
Unit-test saving for correct serialization and graceful handling of storage write exceptions.
Component-test the empty state, addition through button and Enter, trimming, rejection of blank input, and input clearing.
Component-test completion in both directions, targeted deletion, duplicate task text, and deletion of the final task.
Prepopulate localStorage before rendering and verify restored content and completion state. Verify persisted data after add, toggle, and delete operations, then remount to confirm restoration.
Clear localStorage and restore mocks between tests to prevent test-order dependence.
Run npm test and npm run build from the project root and confirm both exit successfully.
Manually check narrow and desktop layouts, long text wrapping, keyboard operation, and persistence across a real browser reload.
risks: Existing project configuration may require adapting the suggested file structure or test setup; avoid replacing working tooling.
Browser storage can be blocked, cleared, or exceed quota, so persistence is best effort when storage operations fail.
Incorrect initialization order can erase saved tasks; lazy loading and restoration tests must guard against this.
Multiple open tabs can overwrite each other's changes; cross-tab synchronization is outside the requested scope.
